The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, has reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to strengthening indigenous shipping capacity, assuring Nigerian shipowners of sustained support and promising his commitment to the disbursement of the Cabotage Vessel Financing Fund to qualified applicants. Oyetola gave the assurance last week in Lagos at the Third Quarter 2026 Citizens’ and Stakeholders’ Engagement of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy. The minister said the administration remained committed to the effective implementation of the Coastal and Inland Shipping Act to ensure that Nigerians participate fully in the ownership and operation of vessels engaged in domestic maritime trade. “To our indigenous shipowners, I wish to reaffirm this administration’s commitment to the development of indigenous shipping capacity and the effective implementation of the Coastal and Inland Shipping (Cabotage) Act,” he said. As part of efforts to address longstanding concerns over access to financing, Oyetola disclosed that he had directed the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency to work closely with approved Primary Lending Institutions to accelerate the processing and disbursement of the Cabotage Vessel Financing Fund to eligible beneficiaries. According to him, the CVFF is regarded as a critical financing instrument for supporting Nigerian shipowners and expanding indigenous participation in the maritime industry. Oyetola stated that its effective deployment was expected to strengthen the national fleet and improve local capacity to compete in the domestic shipping market. He stressed that developing indigenous shipping capacity remained central to the government’s broader objective of ensuring that Nigerians derive greater economic benefits from the country’s maritime resources. “The effective deployment of the CVFF has the potential to strengthen our indigenous fleet and stimulate investment across the maritime value chain,” Oyetola said. The minister also highlighted the importance of professional training, local expertise development, support for indigenous businesses and strategic investment in building a competitive domestic maritime industry. “Our ultimate objective is to build an industry in which Nigerians possess the opportunities, capabilities and resources to own, operate and lead,” he added. Earlier, the Ambassador of the Embassy of the Kingdom of Denmark in Nigeria, Jens Hansen, gave a presentation on Denmark’s Experience in Building a Sustainable Blue Economy: Lessons for Strategic Partnerships, Investment and Technology Transfer with Nigeria at the event.
